labs.name: South Dakota Public Health Laboratory
labs.address: Laboratory Building, 615 East Fourth Street, Pierre, SD 57501
labs.detail: Certified for (as printed by DANR): "Inorganics, SOC's, VOC's, Chlorite, HAA5, Perchlorate, TTHM's, Microbiology, E.Coli enumeration, Chlorite". DANR lists it as "South Dakota State Health Laboratory"; the Department of Health now calls it the South Dakota Public Health Laboratory and gives the same street address (615 E 4th Street, Pierre). Toll-free 1-800-738-2301 (in SD only), per DOH.
labs.source_name: SD DANR Drinking Water Program: Laboratory Certification (web page, no revision date printed)
labs.note: This is the state lab, and it tests private wells. The Department of Health says private persons need "a testing kit from the Department of Health or a special location"; its online Sample Bottle Order Form offers Bacteria/Nitrate, Lead, New Well and Other bottles, and says "Sample bottles and instructions are also available from County Extension offices." DOH's Environmental Testing Fees page (content last updated September 22, 2026) lists, per test: Total Coliform $20.00, E. coli $22.00, Nitrate $18.00, Arsenic $23.00, Lead $18.50, Copper $18.50, Iron $18.00, Manganese $18.00, Sulfate $17.00, Fluoride $16.00, Chloride $16.00, pH $12.00, Conductivity $12.00, Dissolved solids $18.00, Hardness $15.00 (no charge if calcium and magnesium are ordered), Selenium $23.00, Uranium $26.00, Gross alpha/beta $55.00, Radium-226 $85.00, Radium-228 $170.00; organics (pesticides, VOCs): "Contact the Lab". The page does not say which of these a Bacteria/Nitrate bottle is billed as; DOH says fee information comes with the bottles. DOH also says the lab has moved into a new facility and is "fully operational".
labs.source_name_2: SD Department of Health: Test a Private Well, Environmental Testing and Environmental Testing Fees pages (content last updated 2026-10-05 / 2026-09-22; fetched 2026-11-21)

labs.name: Sioux Falls Public Health Laboratory
labs.address: 521 North Main, Suite 100, Sioux Falls, SD 57104
labs.source_name: SD DANR Drinking Water Program: Laboratory Certification (web page, no revision date printed)
labs.note: The City of Sioux Falls says its Public Health Laboratory's testing "serves Falls Community Health, city departments, agencies, commercial businesses, private citizens, and the State of South Dakota," and its page links "How to Collect Water Samples - Well and Household" and a Water Testing Data Form. DANR lists it for microbiology only, so it is a bacteria option, not a nitrate one. The city page does not post fees or hours; call first.
labs.source_name_2: City of Sioux Falls: Health Laboratory page (read 2026-11-21; returns 403 to scripted fetch)

labs.name: Mid Continent Testing Laboratory
labs.address: 2381 South Plaza Drive, PO Box 3388, Rapid City, SD 57709
labs.detail: Certified for (as printed by DANR): "Inorganics, VOC's, Cyanide, Microbiology, E.Coli enumeration,TTHM's, HAA5's, SOC's (except 548 and PCB's), TOCs".
labs.source_name: SD DANR Drinking Water Program: Laboratory Certification (web page, no revision date printed)
labs.note: Mid Continent's Private Well Testing page says its staff "is always prepared to help residential customers with well water testing," and explains bacteria, nitrate, sodium, sulfate, conductivity and common-ion results. It also has a New Well Sampling Program form that it says it supplies to the State with your results, to comply with the 1989 new-well testing law. No prices are posted; call 605-348-0111. The lab's site gives the mailing address as P.O. Box 3388 and fax 605-721-0265.
